newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-REAL BEAT DEPORTIVO AND INCREASE ROBSON'S PROBLEMS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-REAL BEAT DEPORTIVO AND INCREASE ROBSON'S PROBLEMS.

text.p: Real Madrid stretched their lead over Barcelona at the top of the Spanish first division to five points on Sunday after twice coming from behind to beat Deportivo Coruna 3-2.

The result added to the problems of Barcelona coach Bobby Robson, who was summoned to meet club president Jose Luis Nunez after seeing his side throw away a 2-0 lead at home for the second time in less than a month in the 2-2 draw with Oviedo.
There were angry scenes in the Camp Nou after the game, which Barcelona looked to have sewn up just 15 minutes from time.
Juan Pizzi had put the home team ahead shortly after coming on as substitute early in the second half, before Brazilian striker Ronaldo increased the lead with his 19th goal of the season.
But Oviedo's Oli Alvarez pulled one back in the 75th minute and scored the equaliser on the stroke of full time.

"We left Oli unmarked for two headers ... we lost two points, although over the 90 minutes we were the better side. It's a stupid result," said Robson, who refused to answer questions about his meeting with Nunez.
Real Madrid -- who must turn round a 3-2 first leg defeat in Thursday's fourth round Cup tie with Barcelona -- warmed up in fine style by clinching a tough game against Deportivo.
Deportivo took an early lead when Flavio Conceicao gave keeper Bodo Illgner no chance after latching onto a through ball from fellow Brazilian Rivaldo.
Moments later former AC Milan defender Christian Panucci connected with a corner from Roberto Carlos to score his first goal for Real.
Television replays suggested the corner may have left the area of play before swerving back in -- in a repeat of a Panucci goal disallowed in Real's game at Atletico three weeks ago.
Real took control after the break, but it was Deportivo who took the lead when Corentin Martins blasted home a loose ball after Illgner had twice been forced to clear his lines.
Again the lead lasted just a few moments. Fernando Hierro, who scored a magnificent set-piece effort in the Barcelona game, repeated the feat to curl in the equaliser from a free-kick.

Hyperactive Brazilian international Roberto Carlos set up the winner with a move down the left. His cross found Raul Gonzalez, and the teenager kept his head to pass back to Davor Suker, who made no mistake.
Real chairman Lorenzo Sanz acknowledged the quality of Deportivo.
"They're the best side to come to the Bernabeu stadium this season," said Sanz, whose next home game will be against Real Betis.
Betis consolidated their third place five points behind Barcelona with an impressive 3-0 win at Athletic Bilbao. Striker Alfonso Perez was again the dominant figure.
Real Sociedad took fourth ahead of Deportivo after a sensational comeback to win 3-2 after trailing 2-0 with just six minutes on the clock at beleaguered Sevilla.
"Someone else should come, it's no problem for me" said Sevilla manager Jose Antonio Camacho afterwards. Camacho has already had one attempt to resign rejected this season.

Another late goal gave Zaragoza a vital 2-1 victory at fellow strugglers, Logrones. Zaragoza are still third from bottom -- in a season in which four teams face automatic relegation -- but are now level on 18 points with two other sides.
